definitionEn: a person, group or country that supports you when others oppose you
situation: Talking about someone who is on your side and helps you in an argument, competition or conflict.

examples.text: When the board wanted to close our department, the finance director became our strongest [[ally]] and argued to keep it open.
The two countries have been close [[allies]] since the end of the Second World War.
Parents of teenagers should see teachers as [[allies]], not enemies.

texts: She found an unexpected [[ally]] in her former boss.
Regular exercise is your best [[ally]] against stress.
The senator lost her closest [[ally]] when he retired.

badCollocation.noteRu: Школьный друг — a school friend. Ally — союзник в борьбе или споре, а не просто приятель.

collocationTask.prompt: a close ___ of the prime minister
collocationTask.explanationRu: Соратник политика, который его поддерживает, — a close ally. Alliance и union — союзы, а не люди, а partisan — «партизан» или «ярый сторонник партии».

nuance.text: Over the years, the two leaders became close personal [[allies]].
nuance.explanationRu: Ally — союзник, то есть сторона: человек или страна. Alliance — сам союз, соглашение о сотрудничестве; человек не может быть alliance.

reverse.text: The treaty created a military [[alliance]] between four states.
reverse.explanationRu: Договор создаёт союз — an alliance. Ally — участник союза, а не сам союз.

fixIt.text: In the fight to save the local library, the mayor proved a useful [[companion]].
fixIt.explanationRu: Companion — спутник, компаньон в поездке или в жизни. Тот, кто помогает в борьбе за общую цель, — an ally.

reply.context: Your colleague says: "I want to propose a four-day week at the meeting, but I'm scared nobody will back me."
options: Don't worry, I'll be your ally and vote against it with everyone else.
One must endeavour to secure allies prior to submitting such a proposal.
Talk to Sam from HR first. She's been pushing for flexible hours, so she'd be a natural ally.
reply.explanationRu: Ally — тот, кто на вашей стороне, а не голосует против. Второй ответ звучит как учебник по дипломатии, а не дружеский совет.

definitionEn: a light, silver-coloured metal used for cans, foil and aircraft parts
situation: Talking about a light metal used for drink cans, kitchen foil, window frames or parts of planes.

examples.text: Drinks cans made of [[aluminium]] can be recycled again and again without losing quality.
Car makers are switching from steel to [[aluminium]] to make vehicles lighter.
We replaced the old wooden window frames with [[aluminium]] ones that never need painting.

texts: Wrap the fish in [[aluminium]] foil before putting it on the barbecue.
The bike's light [[aluminium]] frame makes it easy to carry upstairs.
Recycling [[aluminium]] uses far less energy than producing it from ore.

badCollocation.noteRu: Тонкая кухонная фольга — aluminium foil (разговорно tin foil). Aluminium paper по-английски не говорят.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Кухонная фольга — aluminium foil (разговорно tin foil). Из железа, меди и стали фольгу для еды не делают.

nuance.text: Most drinks cans today are made of [[aluminium]], which is light and easy to recycle.
nuance.explanationRu: Банки для напитков делают из алюминия — aluminium. Tin — олово; в британском английском a tin — ещё и консервная банка, но она из жести, а не из олова.

reverse.text: Open a [[tin]] of tomatoes and add it to the sauce.
reverse.explanationRu: Консервная банка в британском английском — a tin (в американском — a can). Aluminium — металл, а не упаковка.

fixIt.text: Most modern planes are built mainly from [[tin]] and other light metals.
fixIt.explanationRu: Tin — олово, для самолётов оно не годится. Лёгкий металл для корпусов самолётов — aluminium.

definitionEn: doing an activity for pleasure rather than as a paid job
senseNote: Здесь — «любительский, не за деньги»; неодобрительное «дилетантский» чаще передают словом amateurish.
situation: Describing people who paint, act, play sport or take photos for fun, not to earn money.

examples.text: The play was performed by an [[amateur]] theatre group, but the acting was surprisingly good.
He played [[amateur]] football for years before a professional club finally signed him.
Two [[amateur]] astronomers, a teacher and a retired plumber, spotted the comet before any observatory did.

texts: My uncle is a keen [[amateur]] photographer who enters every local competition.
The race is open to [[amateur]] cyclists of all ages.
She sings with an [[amateur]] choir that meets every Tuesday evening.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Любитель джаза» — a jazz fan или a jazz lover. Amateur — тот, кто сам занимается делом непрофессионально, а не поклонник.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Amateur dramatics — любительский театр, «самодеятельность». Hobby, private и fan с dramatics не сочетаются.

nuance.text: The club is proud of its [[amateur]] status: nobody, not even the coach, gets paid.
nuance.explanationRu: Amateur — нейтральное «любительский, не за деньги». Amateurish — «дилетантский, неумелый», это критика; к статусу клуба без зарплат не подходит.

fixIt.text: My father is a keen [[amateurish]] photographer who spends every weekend in the hills.
fixIt.explanationRu: Amateurish — «дилетантский, неумелый», это критика. Фотограф-любитель — an amateur photographer.

wordFormation.text: The logo looks rather [[amateurish]], as if someone drew it in five minutes.

reply.context: At a dinner party, someone asks you: "So, are you a professional musician?"
options: No, I'm an amateur of classical music: I listen to it every day.
Negative; my musical engagements are strictly of an amateur nature, madam.
No, I just play the cello in an amateur orchestra at weekends, for fun.
reply.explanationRu: Amateur orchestra — любительский оркестр, где играют не за деньги. «Любитель музыки» — music lover, а не amateur of music. Второй ответ слишком чопорный для ужина.

rewrite.original: She plays golf for fun and doesn't get paid for it.
rewrite.explanationRu: An amateur golfer — игрок-любитель, который не получает денег за игру.

definitionEn: a well-known person who represents and promotes a company, cause or activity
senseNote: Здесь — «представитель, лицо» бренда или идеи (brand ambassador); основное значение «посол страны» считаем уже известным.
situation: Talking about a famous or respected person chosen to promote a brand, charity, sport or good cause.

examples.text: The sportswear company hired a young tennis star as its new brand [[ambassador]].
The actress became a goodwill [[ambassador]] for a children's charity and visited refugee camps in three countries.
Our university trains older students as [[ambassadors]] who show new students around the campus.

texts: The former champion is now an [[ambassador]] for women's football.
Every satisfied customer becomes an [[ambassador]] for your brand.
The famous chef acts as an [[ambassador]] for healthy school meals.

badCollocation.noteRu: Посол в стране — ambassador to France, а представитель бренда или идеи — ambassador for the brand или brand ambassador.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Знаменитость, которая представляет бренд, — brand ambassador. Consul, messenger и deputy с brand не сочетаются.

nuance.text: The bank pays the tennis player to act as its [[ambassador]] at tournaments.
nuance.explanationRu: Ambassador — человек, который представляет компанию и продвигает её имидж. Sponsor — тот, кто даёт деньги; здесь спонсор — сам банк, а не теннисист.

reverse.text: A local bakery is the main [[sponsor]] of our school's charity run.
reverse.explanationRu: Кто финансирует мероприятие — sponsor. Ambassador представляет и продвигает его, а не платит.

fixIt.text: The famous skier works as an [[embassy]] for a ski-equipment brand.
fixIt.explanationRu: Embassy — посольство, учреждение. Человек, который представляет бренд, — ambassador.

definitionEn: to make small changes to a law, document or plan to improve it
situation: Changing the wording of a law, contract, report or plan, usually to correct or improve it.

examples.text: Parliament voted to [[amend]] the law so that it also covers online shopping.
We [[amended]] the contract to give freelancers thirty days to submit their invoices.
Please [[amend]] the spelling of my surname on the certificate before it is printed.

texts: The rules were [[amended]] to allow dogs in the park.
She [[amended]] her statement after seeing the video evidence.
The recipe has been [[amended]] to use less sugar.

badCollocation.noteRu: Технику чинят — repair или fix the washing machine. Amend — вносить правки в текст, закон или план.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Поправки в конституцию или закон вносят глаголом amend. Repair — «чинить», correct — «исправлять ошибку», edit — «редактировать текст».

nuance.text: The government plans to [[amend]] the tax code to support small farms.
nuance.explanationRu: Amend — официально изменить закон или документ, чтобы улучшить его. Correct — исправить ошибку, а налоговый кодекс здесь не ошибочен: его дополняют.

reverse.text: The teacher [[corrected]] the spelling mistakes in red ink.
reverse.explanationRu: Исправить ошибки — correct mistakes. Amend меняет документ или закон, а не отдельные ошибки учеников.

fixIt.text: The club decided to [[repair]] its rules so that members can vote online.
fixIt.explanationRu: Repair — «чинить» вещи. Внести изменения в правила — amend the rules.

reply.context: A customer emails: "Sorry, I put the wrong delivery address on my order yesterday."
options: No problem, I've amended your parcel, so it's now much heavier.
No problem at all. I've amended the address, so the parcel will go to the right place.
reply.explanationRu: Amend — исправить или изменить данные, например адрес в заказе. Посылку «исправить» так нельзя, а третий ответ слишком грубый для письма клиенту.

rewrite.original: The government changed the law slightly last year.
rewrite.explanationRu: Нужен пассив: the law was amended.

definitionEn: a change or addition to a law, contract or official document
situation: Talking about an official change added to a law, constitution or contract after a vote or agreement.

examples.text: The opposition proposed an [[amendment]] that would protect small shops from the new tax.
Any [[amendments]] to this contract must be agreed in writing by both parties.
The editor accepted the article after I made a few minor [[amendments]] to the conclusion.

texts: The [[amendment]] was passed by a narrow majority.
Freedom of speech is protected by the First [[Amendment]] in the United States.
The tenant asked for an [[amendment]] allowing her to keep a cat.

badCollocation.noteRu: Поправка к закону — an amendment to the law, а не for the law.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Поправка к конституции — a constitutional amendment. Correction — исправление ошибки, repair — ремонт, patch — «заплатка»; с constitutional так не говорят.

nuance.text: The council voted to add an [[amendment]] banning cars from the old town.
nuance.explanationRu: Amendment — поправка к закону или документу. Amends (make amends) — «загладить вину», это совсем другое слово.

reverse.text: He bought her flowers to make [[amends]] for forgetting her birthday.
reverse.explanationRu: Загладить вину — make amends for something. Amendment — поправка к тексту, к извинениям отношения не имеет.

fixIt.text: The union asked for two [[corrections]] to the contract guaranteeing paid overtime.
fixIt.explanationRu: Correction — исправление ошибки. Поправки, которые меняют условия договора, — amendments.

wordFormation.text: The senator's [[amendment]] would raise the minimum wage for farm workers.

reply.context: In a meeting, your boss asks: "The client has read our proposal. Any news?"
options: They like it overall, but they've asked for a couple of amendments to the budget section.
They loved it so much that they sent us an amendment of flowers.
Affirmative. Amendments have been requested pertaining to the budgetary provisions thereof.
reply.explanationRu: Amendments — поправки, изменения в документе. «Поправка из цветов» — бессмыслица, а третий ответ звучит как юридическая справка, а не ответ начальнику.

definitionEn: during or surrounded by, especially a difficult or noisy situation
situation: Reporting that something happened while there was noise, tension, crisis or strong public feeling around it.

examples.text: The company's shares fell sharply [[amid]] fears of a global recession.
She managed to finish her essay [[amid]] the noise of builders drilling next door.
The team celebrated [[amid]] cheering crowds as the bus drove through the city.

texts: The minister resigned [[amid]] growing criticism of her decisions.
Flights were cancelled [[amid]] concerns about the approaching storm.
The talks ended [[amid]] angry scenes outside the building.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Среди друзей» — among my friends. Amid обычно ставят перед шумом, событиями и настроениями: amid the chaos, amid fears.

collocationTask.prompt: Prices rose ___ fears of a poor harvest.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Amid fears of — «на фоне опасений». Between — «между двумя», inside — «внутри», across — «через, по всей»; с fears так не говорят.

nuance.text: The festival went ahead [[amid]] heavy rain and strong winds.
nuance.explanationRu: Amid — «среди, на фоне» шума, погоды, событий и настроений. Among — «среди» людей или предметов, которых можно посчитать: among friends, among the trees.

reverse.text: The prize money was shared [[among]] the five winners.
reverse.explanationRu: Разделить что-то между несколькими людьми — share among them. Amid с людьми, между которыми что-то делят, не употребляют.

fixIt.text: Share prices fell [[among]] fears of a new trade war.
fixIt.explanationRu: Among ставят перед группой людей или предметов. «На фоне опасений» — amid fears.

rewrite.original: The festival was cancelled because people were worried about safety.
rewrite.frame: The festival was cancelled ____ safety concerns.
rewrite.explanationRu: Amid concerns — «на фоне опасений», типичный оборот новостей.

definitionEn: a comparison that explains one thing by showing how it resembles another
situation: Explaining a difficult idea by comparing it to something simpler that works in a similar way.

examples.text: Our teacher used the [[analogy]] of a busy motorway to explain how blood flows through arteries.
Comparing a start-up to a family is a weak [[analogy]], because employees can be fired.
Journalists often draw an [[analogy]] between the current crisis and the economic collapse of 1929.

texts: The author uses a cooking [[analogy]] to explain how computer programs work.
By [[analogy]] with other planets, scientists expect to find water there.
I don't think your football [[analogy]] really works for a business meeting.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Дешёвый аналог лекарства» — a cheaper equivalent (или analogue). Analogy — сравнение для объяснения, а не похожий товар.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Провести аналогию — draw (или make) an analogy. Pull, do и put с analogy не сочетаются.

nuance.text: The lecturer used an [[analogy]] to explain the idea: the brain as a busy airport.
nuance.explanationRu: Analogy — сравнение, которое мы специально используем, чтобы объяснить мысль. Similarity — просто сходство между вещами; «использовать сходство для объяснения» так не говорят.

reverse.text: There is a striking [[similarity]] between the two sisters' voices.
reverse.explanationRu: Сходство голосов — similarity. Analogy — не само сходство, а сравнение, которое кто-то проводит, чтобы что-то объяснить.

fixIt.text: The professor drew an interesting [[analogue]] between memory and a library.
fixIt.explanationRu: Analogue — «аналог», похожий предмет или продукт. Провести сравнение для объяснения — draw an analogy.

wordFormation.text: The situation is [[analogous]] to a traffic jam: everyone moves slowly because everyone else does.

reply.context: A friend who is learning to code says: "I still don't understand what a database actually is."
options: Here's an analogy: think of it as a huge, well-organised filing cabinet.
An analogy is when a database stores your passwords.
Allow me to furnish you with an illustrative analogy of considerable sophistication.
reply.explanationRu: Analogy — сравнение, которое помогает понять сложное через простое. Во втором ответе слово объяснено неверно, а третий звучит слишком напыщенно для разговора с другом.

definitionEn: to base something firmly on facts, experience or a fixed point
senseNote: Здесь — переносное «прочно опираться, основываться на чём-то» (be anchored in facts); морское «бросать якорь» — базовое значение.
situation: Saying that an idea, story, plan or price is firmly based on or tied to something solid.

examples.text: Although it contains magic, the novel is [[anchored]] in real events from the 1930s.
A good presentation [[anchors]] every claim in clear evidence from real customers.
The central bank has [[anchored]] the currency to the US dollar to keep prices stable.

texts: Her confidence is [[anchored]] in years of hard practice.
The film's fantasy world feels [[anchored]] in everyday family life.
Every decision we make is [[anchored]] in the needs of our patients.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Закрепить пройденный материал» — consolidate или reinforce what you've learned. Anchor в этом учебном смысле не употребляют.

collocationTask.explanationRu: О том, что прочно опирается на факты, говорят firmly anchored (или grounded) in reality. Fastened, nailed и glued — о креплении предметов.

nuance.text: Good policy should be [[anchored]] in evidence, not in guesswork.
nuance.explanationRu: Anchored in evidence — «опирается на факты». Attach — «прикреплять» предмет или «привязаться» к человеку; attached in evidence не говорят.

reverse.text: I've become very [[attached]] to my old car.
reverse.explanationRu: Эмоционально привязаться — become attached to. Anchored говорит об опоре и основании, а не о чувствах.

fixIt.text: His arguments are always [[fixed]] in solid data, which makes them hard to dismiss.
fixIt.explanationRu: Fixed — «закреплённый, неподвижный». Опираться на данные — be anchored in data.

definitionEn: with a name that is not known or not made public
senseNote: Здесь — «анонимный, неназванный»; значение «безликий, невыразительный» (an anonymous hotel room) не тренируем.
situation: Describing a person, letter, gift or comment when nobody knows or reveals who it came from.

examples.text: The letter was [[anonymous]], so the police had no idea who had sent it.
The staff survey is completely [[anonymous]], so be honest about your manager.
Some people post cruel comments online because they feel safe being [[anonymous]].

texts: A generous [[anonymous]] donor paid for the new library.
The journalist spoke to an [[anonymous]] source inside the ministry.
Online reviews can be [[anonymous]], so treat them with caution.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Остаться анонимным» — remain или stay anonymous. Keep anonymous без дополнения звучит неестественно.

collocationTask.prompt: The winner has asked to ___ anonymous.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Остаться анонимным — remain (или stay) anonymous. Keep, hold и save в этом значении без дополнения не используют.

nuance.text: The donor asked to stay [[anonymous]], so the charity cannot reveal his name.
nuance.explanationRu: Anonymous — человек сознательно не называет своё имя. Unknown — «неизвестный, малоизвестный», и попросить «остаться unknown» по-английски так не говорят.

reverse.text: The film stars a young actor who was completely [[unknown]] until last year.
reverse.explanationRu: Никому не известный, не знаменитый — unknown. Anonymous значит, что имя скрыто, а не что человек не знаменит.

fixIt.text: The police received an [[incognito]] phone call about the stolen paintings.
fixIt.explanationRu: Incognito — о человеке, который скрывает, кто он (travel incognito). Звонок от неизвестного — an anonymous call.

wordFormation.text: Journalists must protect the [[anonymity]] of their sources.

reply.context: Your manager says: "We're running a survey about workload. Will you fill it in?"
options: Sure, as long as it's anonymous and has my name and photo on it.
Affirmative, provided that the anonymity of respondents is duly guaranteed.
Of course. Will it be anonymous? People might be more honest if it is.
reply.explanationRu: Anonymous — без имени, поэтому анкета «с именем и фото» анонимной не будет. Второй ответ звучит как договор, а не ответ начальнику.

rewrite.original: The person who gave the money did not want anyone to know her name.
